newsitem.title: UK: Mirror expanding in English Midlands.
newsitem.headline: Mirror expanding in English Midlands.

text.p: Britain's Mirror Group Plc announced an expansion into the English local press on Friday through a 297 million pound ($501 million) agreed bid for Midland Independent Newspapers (MIN).

National newspaper group Mirror spent more than 70 million pounds acquiring 34.45 million MIN shares at 210 pence each to build an initial stake of some 25 percent. The deal is an important strategic move for Mirror which has regional newspapers in Scotland and Northern Ireland and is now driving into the heart of England.
Mirror shares rose 14.5p to 200.5 on Friday as share analysts welcomed the deal while MIN added 6.5p to 195p.
"We are confident that the acquisition of MIN will make a positive and significant contribution to Mirror Group's future growth prospects," said Mirror chief executive David Montgomery.
Mirror said the deal should provide benefits from shared resources, distribution and advertising. It said an initial five million pounds could be cut from costs.

MIN publishes 44 newspaper titles, including dailies The Birmingham Post and Birmingham Evening Mail in England's second city. Mirror and MIN have agreed a price of 210 pence per share, around the level analysts had expected Mirror to have to pay for Britain's sixth largest regional newspaper publisher.
Analysts said the expansion was a logical one and that a strong performance from MIN in the first half of the year made the price seem acceptable.
"Newspapers are what Mirror does well," said Colin Tennant of UBS.
"MIN is doing a bit better trading wise than expected, Mirror says it can cut costs by five million pounds almost immediately and so they can probably make it earnings enhancing from 1998," he added.
Mirror Group's flagship tabloid newspaper is Britain's second best selling daily after Rupert Murdoch's Sun. The company also owns popular Scottish titles the Daily Record and Sunday Mail.
It has recently branched out into cable television through its LIVE TV operation but media ownership laws prevent it from playing a major role in the commercial terrestrial television (ITV) sector.

English local newspapers have long been seen as a likely area for Mirror to move into and speculation linking it with MIN, its partner in the Birmingham Live local cable TV channel, has been rife for months.

MIN, a management buy-out from U.S. publisher Ralph Ingersoll in 1991, forecast profit before tax and exceptional items of at least 13.2 million pounds in the first half of the year against 8.3 million a year ago.

Chris Oakley, the MIN chief executive whose stake in the company is worth some 4.5 million pounds, will join the Mirror board when the deal goes through. It is subject to regulatory approval and the green light is not expected before October.
